mcqs.question: If \(P(x)=3x^{3}-2x^{2}+5x-7\) and \(Q(x)=x^{3}+4x^{2}-2x+3\), what is \(P(x)-Q(x)\)?
mcqs.explanation: When subtracting \(Q(x)\) from \(P(x)\) we change the sign of every term of \(Q(x)\): \(P(x)-Q(x) = (3x^{3}-2x^{2}+5x-7) - (x^{3}+4x^{2}-2x+3) = 3x^{3}-x^{3} -2x^{2}-4x^{2} +5x+2x -7-3 = 2x^{3}-6x^{2}+7x-10. Option B forgets to change the sign of \(-2x\) and gives 3x instead of 7x. Options C and D contain multiple sign errors.

mcqs.question: Combine like terms in the expression: \(4x^{2}+3xy-5x+2x^{2}-xy+7\).
mcqs.explanation: Group the same powers and same variables: \(4x^{2}+2x^{2}=6x^{2}\); \(3xy-xy=2xy\); \(-5x\) stays unchanged; constant term is 7. Hence the simplified form is \(6x^{2}+2xy-5x+7\). Option B adds an extra \(xy\), Option C misses the \(x^{2}\) terms, and Option D changes the sign of \(-5x\).

mcqs.question: Which of the following expressions is written in standard form with terms arranged in descending powers of \(x\)?
mcqs.explanation: Standard form lists terms from the highest exponent to the lowest. Option A follows the order \(x^{4}, x^{2}, x^{1}, x^{0}\). Option B starts with \(x^{2}\), Option C places the constant before the \(x^{2}\) term, and Option D puts the constant before the \(x\) term, breaking the descending order.

mcqs.question: Simplify the expression: \((2x^{3}-4x^{2}+6x) - (x^{3}+5x^{2}-2x) + (3x^{2}-x)\).
mcqs.explanation: First distribute the minus sign: \( (2x^{3}-4x^{2}+6x) - x^{3} -5x^{2}+2x +3x^{2}-x\). Combine like terms: \(2x^{3}-x^{3}=x^{3}\); \(-4x^{2}-5x^{2}+3x^{2}= -6x^{2}\); \(6x+2x- x =7x\). The simplified result is \(x^{3}-6x^{2}+7x\). Options B and C have incorrect coefficients for the \(x^{2}\) or \(x\) terms, and D retains the original \(2x^{3}\) instead of subtracting correctly.
